name: Kilkenny
tagline: A genuinely well-preserved medieval city, its castle and cathedral still anchoring streets laid out nearly a thousand years ago.
highlight: Walking the Medieval Mile from the castle to St Canice's Cathedral as the round tower comes into view above the rooftops.
shortDescription: A compact, exceptionally well-preserved medieval city in southeast Ireland, anchored by its castle, a 6th-century round tower and a genuine brewing heritage.
metaDescription: A Kilkenny travel guide: Kilkenny Castle, St Canice's Cathedral, Rothe House, food and how to plan a visit to Ireland's best-preserved medieval city.

image.alt: Kilkenny Castle overlooking the River Nore

intro: Kilkenny is genuinely Ireland's best-preserved medieval city, its narrow streets still following a layout laid out under Norman rule nearly a thousand years ago.

The city's skyline is genuinely anchored by two landmarks from very different eras — the Anglo-Norman Kilkenny Castle overlooking the River Nore, and St Canice's 6th-century round tower rising above the cathedral quarter, one of the few in Ireland still open for visitors to climb.
Most visitors genuinely explore it as an easy day trip or overnight from Dublin, walking the signposted Medieval Mile between the city's historic sites at an unhurried pace.

whyVisit.intro: Kilkenny's case rests on genuinely dense, walkable medieval history rarely matched elsewhere in Ireland.

points.title: It's genuinely Ireland's best-preserved medieval city
points.text: Streets and buildings still follow a layout largely unchanged since Norman times.

points.title: St Canice's Round Tower is genuinely climbable
points.text: A rare 6th-century round tower where visitors can still climb to the top for city views.

points.title: Kilkenny Castle is genuinely a full afternoon on its own
points.text: Restored state rooms and formal gardens right in the city centre.

points.title: It's genuinely a real brewing town
points.text: Home to Smithwick's, Ireland's oldest operating brewery, with a genuine history to match.

points.title: It works genuinely well as an easy Dublin day trip
points.text: A little over an hour by train, making it accessible even on a short Ireland itinerary.

attractionsIntro: Kilkenny's essential sights are genuinely dense enough to cover comfortably on foot along the signposted Medieval Mile.

attractions.name: Kilkenny Castle

image.alt: Kilkenny Castle overlooking the River Nore

attractions.text: Genuinely the city's dominant landmark, a Norman-founded castle rebuilt over centuries, with restored state rooms open to visitors.
attractions.tip: Book genuinely the state apartments tour ahead in summer — the castle's grounds themselves are free to explore.

attractions.name: St Canice's Cathedral & Round Tower

image.alt: St Canice's Cathedral and round tower in Kilkenny

attractions.text: A genuinely striking medieval cathedral beside a rare 6th-century round tower, one of the few in Ireland still open for visitors to climb.
attractions.tip: Climb genuinely the round tower's steep internal ladders for a rewarding view over the whole city.

attractions.name: The Medieval Mile Museum

image.file: File:Graveyard of the Medieval Mile Museum.jpg
image.alt: The Medieval Mile Museum, housed in a former medieval church in Kilkenny

attractions.text: Genuinely housed in a beautifully restored medieval church, telling the city's history through artefacts found along the Medieval Mile itself.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a good first stop to get context before walking the rest of the Mile.

attractions.name: Rothe House

image.alt: Rothe House, a restored Tudor merchant's house in Kilkenny

attractions.text: Genuinely Ireland's most complete surviving Tudor merchant's house, built around three courtyards for a wealthy trading family.
attractions.tip: The genuinely walled garden behind the house has been recreated in a 17th-century style.

attractions.name: Kilkenny Castle's Rose Garden

image.alt: The Rose Garden at Kilkenny Castle

attractions.text: Genuinely formal gardens within the castle's parkland, a peaceful, free-to-enter space right in the city centre.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a good picnic spot on a fine day, with wide lawns beyond the formal beds.

attractions.name: The Smithwick's Experience

image.alt: The Smithwick's Experience brewery visitor centre in Kilkenny

attractions.text: Genuinely tells the story of Ireland's oldest operating brewery, founded on the site of a medieval abbey in 1710.
attractions.tip: The genuinely tour ends with a tasting, included in the ticket price.

attractions.name: Kilkenny's medieval streets
attractions.text: Genuinely narrow lanes like the Butter Slip and High Street still trace the city's original Norman-era layout.
attractions.tip: Genuinely look up — many buildings hide medieval features above modern shopfronts.

thingsToDoIntro: Kilkenny genuinely rewards a slow walk along the Medieval Mile, mixing museums with its brewing heritage.

thingsToDo.title: Climb St Canice's Round Tower

image.alt: The interior of St Canice's Round Tower in Kilkenny

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely rare chance to climb inside a 6th-century round tower, one of only a handful in Ireland still open to visitors.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely not for the claustrophobic — the internal ladders are steep and narrow.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Kilkenny Castle's gardens

image.file: File:Kilkenny Castle Gardens, The Parade, Kilkenny (506850) (28768828550).jpg

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely relaxed way to spend an hour, walking the castle's formal gardens and wider parkland.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely free to enter, even without a ticket for the castle's state apartments.

thingsToDo.title: Learn brewing history at Smithwick's

image.alt: The Smithwick's Experience visitor centre in Kilkenny

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely engaging tour through Ireland's oldest brewery, built on the site of a medieval Franciscan abbey.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely book ahead in summer — tour slots can fill up on busy days.

thingsToDo.title: Browse the Medieval Mile Museum

image.file: File:Interior of the Medieval Mile Museum.jpg
image.alt: Inside the Medieval Mile Museum in Kilkenny

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely worthwhile hour, exploring artefacts and stories from along the city's historic medieval core.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely a good first stop before walking the rest of the Mile yourself.

thingsToDo.title: Walk the full Medieval Mile

image.alt: Rothe House along Kilkenny's Medieval Mile

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely signposted walking route linking the castle, cathedral and the city's best-preserved medieval buildings.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely allow a full afternoon to do the route justice with stops along the way.

thingsToDo.title: Have a pint in a medieval pub
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely atmospheric way to end the day, several of Kilkenny's pubs occupy buildings centuries old.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely ask locally for the oldest pub in town — several make a genuine claim to the title.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Kilkenny?
faq.a: One day genuinely covers the Medieval Mile's main sights comfortably; an overnight allows a more relaxed pace.

faq.q: Can you visit Kilkenny as a day trip from Dublin?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely easily — direct trains take just over ninety minutes each way.
Yes, genuinely — the restored state apartments and free gardens make it worth a couple of hours on their own.
Genuinely its exceptionally well-preserved medieval streets, its castle, and its brewing heritage at Smithwick's.

faq.q: Can you climb St Canice's Round Tower?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — it's one of the few round towers in Ireland still open to visitors, via a steep internal ladder.

faq.q: Is Kilkenny worth visiting if you're only doing Dublin and one other stop?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — its combination of density and easy access from Dublin makes it one of the best single-day additions to a short Ireland trip.
